text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in Russian newspapers this morning. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
KOMMERSANT DAILY
- President Yeltsin's statement on warheads in Paris puzzled not only his entourage and journalists but also the heads of other states.
- Russia's government once again emphasised its priorities -- economic growth and social protection.
- The government wants to increase individual's payments to the Pension Fund to improve the situation with pensions arrears.
- Prices on land in St Petersburg are to go down significantly.
- Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin is gathering political forces apparently preparing for the 2000 presidential elections.
- Moscow Mayor Yuri Luzhkov calls for protection of national producers and revival of positive elements of the state planning system.
SEVODNYA
- The Russian Black Sea Fleet is likely to be locked up in two bays in Sevastopol.
- Russia's government approved a system of standards which defines the amount of subsidies to the regions from the federal budget.
- The government demonstrated its unity in a carefully planned performance at yesterday's Finance Ministry meeting.
- The cabinet has intensified its work with the country's regions. This move can be regarded as a start of a new regional policy.
- Russian oil company Surgutneftegaz is to increse its charter capital.
- Fuel and Energy Ministry efforts to initiate competition among energy producers will remain void declarations as long as actual tariffs are determined by the federal Energy Commission.
NEZAVISIMAYA GAZETA
- President Yeltsin's sensational statement on dismantling warheads was a gift to NATO. It is not clear what Russia gains in exchange.
- The government's initiatives on cutting social benefits are extremely unpopular with parliament and trade unions.
ROSSIISKAYA GAZETA
- A difficult way to a compromise has been passed, says the paper in comments over the signing of the Founding Act on Russia-NATO relations.
PRAVDA-5
- Russia has received "cheap stuff in an expensive wrapping" says the opposition over the signing of the agreement with NATO.
MOSKOVSKY KOMSOMOLETS
- It is hard to explain why Russia, which has a lot of brilliant polititians and economists, is such a poor country.
-- Svetlana Kovaleva, Moscow Newsroom, +7095 941 8520
